t: Iranian-speaking horse nomads who broke the Scythians and held the steppe from the Volga to the Danube for six centuries.
Not one state but a confederation of tribes such as the Iazyges, Roxolani, Aorsi, Siraces and Alans, each with its own kings.
Their armoured lancers fought and served Rome; the Goths and then the Huns ended their dominance in the 3rd and 4th centuries.
dyk: Herodotus claimed that a Sauromatian girl could not marry until she had killed an enemy in battle, and archaeologists have found many early Sarmatian women buried with weapons.
ev: Sarmatian tribes cross the Don and lay waste much of Scythia
The Sarmatian ruler Gatalos is named in the treaty ending the war of Pharnaces I of Pontus
The Legio III Gallica destroys 9,000 Roxolani raiders in Moesia
A Sarmatian war under Domitian costs Rome a legion
Iazyges king Zanticus makes peace; 5,500 Sarmatian horsemen are sent to Britain
The Limigantes revolt; Constantine settles Sarmatian refugees in the empire
The Huns defeat the Alans and Goths, scattering the Sarmatian peoples
